crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Invoice Capture and Coding
children.blurb: Invoice capture and coding covers the intake of supplier invoices from email, scan, or electronic feed and the conversion of those documents into structured records.

children.name: Customer Credit Risk
children.blurb: Customer credit risk is the chance that a business customer will not pay what it owes under agreed terms, and it sits on the receivables side of payables and receivables.

children.name: Programmable Settlement and Escrow
children.blurb: Programmable settlement and escrow covers the use of software rules to hold, release, and reconcile funds between parties in payables and receivables.

children.name: Collections and Payment Plans
children.blurb: Collections and payment plans cover the work of recovering overdue receivables and structuring scheduled payments, whether a customer needs an installment plan or a vendor needs a revised payables schedule.

children.name: Working Capital Timing
children.blurb: Working capital timing covers when cash actually moves in and out of a business, not just when an invoice is dated.

sections.body: Payables and receivables is the money in and money out side of the finance function, and AI is now doing real work there rather than sitting in a demo. In payables, systems read supplier invoices, pull out line items, tax, and payment terms, then match them to purchase orders and contracts before coding them to the ledger. In receivables, models score customer credit, forecast which invoices will be paid late, and trigger reminders or payment plans. Banks and fintechs use AI to route payments, detect fraud, and in some cases manage escrow conditions. The work is mostly pattern recognition, document understanding, and forecasting, not general reasoning. It touches cash flow every day, so errors have immediate financial consequences.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Document extraction is largely solved for clean, digital invoices, but accuracy drops with poor scans, unusual layouts, handwritten annotations, and mixed languages. Credit risk scoring is widely deployed, yet it depends on historical data that can be thin for small businesses or biased against certain groups. Programmable settlement and escrow exist, but their use is limited by banking rails, legal recognition, and the need for trusted oracles. Collections automation can prioritize accounts and suggest payment plans, but it cannot reliably conduct a difficult negotiation or handle hardship cases without human judgment. Working capital timing models can recommend when to pay or collect, but they are only as good as the cash flow forecast behind them. The honest limit is that most systems still need human review, audit trails, and clear rules for exceptions.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Each page under this section covers one link in that chain. Invoice Capture and Coding is the entry point, where a reader goes to understand how documents become structured ledger data. Customer Credit Risk explains how AI assesses whether a buyer will pay, which feeds decisions across the rest of the section. Programmable Settlement and Escrow looks at the execution layer, where payment conditions are automated or held in trust. Collections and Payment Plans covers what happens after due date, including prioritization, outreach, and structured repayment. Working Capital Timing ties the others together by asking when cash should move to keep the business solvent. A reader can start with any page, but the full picture only appears when they are read as a sequence.
